svg.text: Detailed Class/Interface Model — bookAppointment, cancelAppointment, notification
UC-06, UC-08, UC-09, UC-11 · Readable export of detailed-class-design.mmd · arrows show dependency direction (caller → callee, adapter implements port)

g.text: Ports — interfaces owned by the core

svg.text: Constructor-injected with ports only; no Spring/JPA/HTTP
imports. @Transactional is added in the Spring build (annotation only).
UC-11 · tries senders in priority order; a failing channel
never propagates an exception (booking stays committed)
delivers events only once the booking is committed
reads the service's cut-off, else the University
default (one class; variation is data, not behaviour)

• Dependency rule: no class in the core, domain or ports imports a Spring, JPA, HTTP or SMTP type. Every adapter depends on a port; no port depends on an adapter. The core compiles with the JDK alone.
• DP-1 Repository isolates persistence (UC-06, QS-04). DP-2 domain event keeps notification out of the booking transaction (UC-11, QS-04).
DP-3 Adapter port gives UC-11 an ordered in-app → email fallback. Strategy was rejected for the cancellation cut-off (UC-09): it is a configured value, not varying behaviour.
• Colour key: orange = application services · yellow = domain · green = ports (interfaces) · blue = adapters (framework / external). Solid arrow = uses · dashed hollow-head arrow = implements.
• Participants shown here are the same names as the files in src/interfaces-or-ports/ (ports/, domain/, application/); the blue adapters are implemented in Phase 2 against the same interfaces.
